scenes.text: Hi, we are Team Echo, and this is SurgeSight.
Every cyclone season, India gets good forecasts. They tell us where the storm will go. But a District Collector still has to work out what it will hit: which school, which hospital, which road.
SurgeSight turns one cyclone bulletin into ranked risks, clear reasons and alerts that are ready to approve. It is built on Gemini, Earth Engine and Google Maps.

scenes.chapter: Choose a role and a language
scenes.text: Each officer starts by choosing a role, like Health or Electricity, and a language. From then on, every screen puts their own facilities first.
The live view shows wind, rain, temperature and alert zones across India, from the newest forecast. It refreshes itself every three hours on Cloud Run.
To test it, we replayed Cyclone Michaung, which hit Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh in December 2023.
The overview shows the storm at each bulletin: how strong it is, when it reaches the coast, and the top priorities for the Health department.

On the map, every school, hospital and substation under the storm is scored and coloured by risk. Alert zones move with the storm. You see the observed track, our experimental forecast and its uncertainty, with rain and wind from Earth Engine.

Tap any facility to see why it was alerted. KGVB School in Kothapatnam is critical: three metres above sea level, two hundred and seventy two millimetres of forecast rain, and ninety four kilometres an hour of wind. Gemini explains it in plain words, and every number it writes is checked.
We screened nearly thirty four thousand kilometres of main roads. This page names the roads to check first, and the hospitals whose road access could be cut off.
Affected areas ranks every district by alert level, with its people and facilities.

Gemini then writes an advisory for each department, grounded in these facilities and roads. It works in six Indian languages, here Tamil, with audio and a standard CAP alert. Nothing is sent until an officer approves it.
Settings let every officer change role, language and theme, including a dark mode for the control room at night.
SurgeSight uses twenty three Google services, including Gemini with the Agent Development Kit, Earth Engine, the Maps Platform, BigQuery, Firebase and Cloud Run.
Next, we want to reach every coastal home: a citizen app, alerts to every phone through SACHET, and a model that learns from every storm.
SurgeSight does not replace IMD. It turns forecasts into action before landfall. We are Team Echo. Thank you.
